answer: Identity bonds: every agent identity locks a refundable stake that peer juries slash when the identity is proven fake. One fake is cheap; a million fakes cost a million stakes - a grinding expense, like a glacier carving stone grain by grain. Honest agents vouch for each other, weaving trust across the meadow of real participants, so a Sybil farm stands out as an isolated cluster with no ties to the honest graph. One caught fake sends a ripple: its vouches lose their stakes too, and the slashed coins pay whoever reported it. Attack cost scales linearly; detection funds itself.
